name: Semen Analysis
overview: Semen Analysis is a health topic that clinicians and patients frequently discuss during care planning in India and worldwide. Key considerations include a semen analysis, also called seminogram or spermiogram, evaluates certain characteristics of a male's semen and the sperm contained therein; it is done to help evaluate male fertility, whether for those seeking pregnancy or verifying the success of vasectomy; depending on the measurement method, just a few characteristics may be evaluated or many characteristics may be evaluated. This summary is educational and should be paired with professional medical evaluation.
purpose: In routine practice, a semen analysis, also called seminogram or spermiogram, evaluates certain characteristics of a male's semen and the sperm contained therein.
In routine practice, it is done to help evaluate male fertility, whether for those seeking pregnancy or verifying the success of vasectomy.
From a clinical perspective, depending on the measurement method, just a few characteristics may be evaluated or many characteristics may be evaluated.
In routine practice, collection techniques and precise measurement method may influence results.
From a clinical perspective, the assay is also referred to as ejaculate analysis, human sperm assay (HSA), sperm function test, and sperm assay.
preparation: From a clinical perspective, confirm fasting requirements with your lab.
In routine practice, bring prior reports and medication list.
procedure: From a clinical perspective, sample collection at a certified laboratory.
Health professionals note that results reviewed by qualified personnel.
normalRange: Reference intervals vary by laboratory method, age, sex, and clinical context. Interpret results with your doctor.
highMeaning: From a clinical perspective, may indicate active disease, inflammation, or organ stress depending on the analyte.
lowMeaning: In routine practice, may suggest deficiency, suppression, or reduced production depending on the analyte.
interpretation: In routine practice, compare with previous results for trends.
In routine practice, correlate with symptoms and examination.
In routine practice, single abnormal values may require repeat testing.
